q: he told me he wants to buy a new computer setup worth around ₱150,000. The problem is that the money would come from our shared savings—the same savings that we may need for my upcoming C-section, delivery expenses, and any unexpected costs after the baby arrives.
cx: Philippines, 32 weeks, a planned surgical birth; her husband lost a client.

q: I currently have one main job and one side job, but I’ll be starting my maternity leave at the end of July.
cx: Her own work while pregnant.

q: when I was trying to talk to him and explain why it would be better to postpone this purchase until October—at least two months after my scheduled C-section—he suddenly became cold and distant.
cx: How her husband reacted to waiting on the purchase.

q: The money we’re planning to use for my operation isn’t just his money—it’s also my money through the benefits provided by the company I work for.
cx: Whose money pays for the birth.

q: Last week I asked if I could work remotely because I was in so much pain that I genuinely didn’t think I could make it through the day. I was told that if I couldn’t come in, I would need to use sick time
cx: California, 30 weeks; management cut work-from-home for everyone.

q: I’ve already used most of my sick leave dealing with pregnancy-related health issues and appointments, so hearing that honestly felt like a punch in the gut.
cx: Sick leave already gone before the birth.

q: Getting dressed, rolling over in bed, getting in and out of the car, walking, standing, sitting, everything hurts. I’m lucky if I get four hours of sleep a night.
cx: Pelvic pain at 30 weeks.

q: The next morning, I got a call from a prenatal support specialist through my clinic. She had reviewed the notes from my appointment and was basically like, “Why are we waiting two weeks to discuss this?”
cx: Her clinic's support specialist moved her leave forward.

q: She went over California leave programs (PDL, SDI, CFRA, PFL, all of it).
cx: One phone call that explained the state leave programs.

q: My mom keeps telling me to enjoy these last ten weeks before the baby gets here because I’ll never have this time again. Instead, all I can think about is how not working feels dangerous.
cx: Signed off work at 30 weeks; she grew up poor.

q: My brain immediately jumps to, “What if I lose my job? What if something happens financially? What if everything falls apart?” For me, it feels like not working = bad.
cx: Fear of stopping work early.

q: I haven’t even officially told management yet. It’s not even Monday. And every time I think about sending the email, I start shaking.
cx: Before telling work she is going on leave now.

q: that golden hour is exactly what I would love to have. I think that’s what I feel so robbed off. Not being able to cuddle her for 10 hours.
cx: Thinking about a second baby after a frightening first birth.

q: Sorry I just need somewhere to vent as my husband laughs off every comment I make so it's adding to my frustration.
cx: UK, 40+6 with her second.

q: my first baby came spontaneously on my due date and whilst I know that's extremely rare and lucky, I did use that to mentally prepare myself for this labour and birth
cx: She expected the second birth to follow the first.

q: I am so scared of the intervention it's going to cause and can't help but feel like my body is failing me this time
cx: The day before an appointment to discuss induction.

q: the deflation and disappointment is more than I would have thought.
cx: Overdue for the first time.

q: she would get a new job right after I got pregnant, which (a) means she won’t be entitled to any paid leave when baby #2 comes, and (b) requires her to travel overseas every couple of months for 1 week at a time, leaving me alone with the toddler
cx: UK, 24 weeks; her wife carried their first child.

q: there’s no lying in, taking random naps or long baths when you have an 18 month old.
cx: Why this pregnancy differs from her wife's.

q: I am so excited for this baby but I’m also dreading it because my wife will only get two weeks off (unpaid) and then I’ll be on my own again.
cx: Looking ahead to the newborn weeks.

q: while I am less and less able to lift him, and we are having a heatwave in the UK.
cx: Alone with the toddler when her wife travels.

q: I’ve thrown up at work a few times (I work as an esthetician so this is very frustrating and luckily has only happened when I’m not with a client)
cx: Sickness returned at 17 weeks.

q: I knew it came back for some people in trimester 3, but I’d don’t expect it back so soon 😭😭
cx: Sickness back weeks after it had stopped.

q: I am an independent woman, I have my own money and don't need a man for those things, but I do when on maternity and getting to know my little man once he arrives (I refuse to give up my year with him).
cx: UK, 30 weeks, a strained marriage.

q: I can't nest as the house is still a building zone. It will get done, but we're pushing it.
cx: Third trimester in a heatwave with building work at home.

q: My 2 month old was doing great and I thought I was getting the hang of things. Then the heatwave hit and I realised I don’t know how to keep her safe and happy.
cx: First heatwave with a baby.

q: she needs air in the stroller and I thought that is what the  built in ventilation is for now people tell me that isn’t enough. Now I’m just afraid to take her outside
cx: What she was told about the stroller in the heat.
